                                Scaling Metts(taxi-service) v2

**p1. Goal : 1k per second (10,000 drivers)**

**bottleneck 1\. Inserting into Postgres.**

**Issue:** every coordinate data INSERT to drivers\_locations table therefore it create 50 Transactions on for drivers\_location table . 

Solution 1\. “Redis Batch” coordinates. (insert coordinates only 1 time.)  
INSERT 50 coordinates at once. We are gathering 50 records to package and                  then INSERT to the drivers\_locations table.  
![][image1]

For batching and saving coordinates when order in status “in\_progress” we should use Redis. 

Tradeoffs

- if some coordinates are lost we can’t write it to db and redis will save it forever.  
- redis can be a bottleneck in future.  
- we can’t control load(if 100 orders coordinates will be writing simultaneously to db)

Plus  
	

	  
Solution 2\. Queue Batchering (without Redis)

Using queue and Batchering together. After giving coordinates it writes to the general queue. general queue wait for (example) 1 second or (example) 50 coordinates and then the consumer get message and insert it to db at once.

![][image2]

Tradeoffs

\- Higher latency because messages wait for batching.  
\- Careful ACK handling is required to avoid data loss.  
\- Large batches increase transaction size.  
\- If PostgreSQL is slower than the incoming message rate, RabbitMQ queues will continue growing until consumers catch up.

Plus  
\-  We can control how much message we write per second  
\-  Easily add database sharding / realize go concurency (just add queue / concurrency) for my opinion.

Conclusion: 

During benchmarking, grouping inserts into larger transactions increased throughput from **\~197 inserts/sec** to **\~3931 inserts/sec (\~20x)**. Therefore, batching reduces transaction overhead and increases database write throughput.
